# GEO report: atlas-roadmaps **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 12.58 ÷ 23 × 100 = 55. High = (12.58 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 55. A cap applies, so the score is 40, not 55. The cap applies because your `robots.txt` blocks Bingbot from the whole site, which goes against your own policy of allowing AI search crawlers. Bing's index feeds several AI search tools, so this one line holds the whole score down. Nothing was "Can't tell", so the score is firm for what the code shows. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Bingbot - **Why it matters:** Bing, and tools that use its index, are told to stay out of every page, which contradicts `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`. It also makes your pages count as not indexable. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5-6` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Bingbot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 81/100, Good (the cap is lifted and GEO-009 and GEO-014 both come back Clear). ### 2. Point robots.txt at your sitemap - **Why it matters:** Your `sitemap.xml` exists, but nothing tells crawlers where it is. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt` (no `Sitemap:` line) - **What the code says:** the file ends at `Disallow: /` under `GPTBot`. - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 89/100 with item 1 also done. Alone it reaches 63 but stays capped at 40. ### 3. Give /pricing its own title, description and canonical - **Why it matters:** It has no metadata, so it shows the site-wide "Atlas" title and description, and it has no canonical address. - **Where:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` - **What the code says:** `export default function Pricing() { return

Pricing

…` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** about 59 uncapped, so 40 until item 1 is done. With items 1 and 3 together it is 85. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Problem | `public/robots.txt:5-6` Bingbot blocked site-wide. GPTBot block (line 8) is a training-crawler choice and isn't counted. | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | Bingbot blocked on all 4 routes. No noindex on public pages. `/dashboard` is deliberately noindex and isn't in the sitemap. | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical | Problem | Clear on 3 of 4 routes. `app/routes/pricing.tsx` has none. | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Clear on 3 of 4 routes. `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5` loads entries in `useEffect`. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid but `robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | `lang="en"` is set (`app/root.tsx:5`). Clear on 3 of 4 routes. Pricing falls back to the root default (`app/root.tsx:2`). | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Problem | Clear on 2 of 3 routes. `/features` is reached only by `onClick` (`app/routes/_index.tsx:9`). | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet` in any file I read | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | `root.tsx` and all route files read. No images, links have text. | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | Not a mobile app | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | None present. Not scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | None present. Not scored. | ## Other problems found - **Page reachable only by a click handler:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:9`: `
navigate('/features')}>See all features
`. Replace it with ``. `/features` is not in the main nav either. - **Changelog is empty in the first HTML:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5`: `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/changelog')…`. Load the entries in a Remix `loader` so they are in the served page. ## Worth considering - **Back up the integrations claim:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:8`: `Integrates with all the tools you already use.` Name the actual tools in text, since visitors will want to know whether yours is on the list. - **Say what plans cost:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`: `Talk to us for a quote.` Add plan names, what each includes and prices, or a range, if you can share them. - **Add Organization/WebSite structured data:** no JSON-LD exists, and `app/root.tsx` is where it would go. It would state the name "Atlas" and the origin `https://atlasroadmaps.example` in a machine-readable way. - **Add `` dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has none. The changelog has real release dates you could use. - **Give changelog releases their own pages:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:6` renders every entry as a list item. Per-release addresses would let people link to and cite a specific release. - **Add charset and viewport tags:** `app/root.tsx:6` has only ``, and neither tag is set in `meta`. - **Put the nav in the layout for every key page:** `app/root.tsx:7` links Pricing and Changelog but not Features or the home page. Add Features. - **Make the Features page say more:** `app/routes/features.tsx:1` promises "Timelines, sharing and status updates" in one sentence. A short section on each would answer what a visitor comes to learn. - **Improve the root fallback metadata:** `app/root.tsx:2`: `{ title: 'Atlas' }` doesn't say what Atlas is. Use something like "Atlas: roadmaps for product teams". - **Disallow plus noindex on /dashboard:** `public/robots.txt:3` blocks crawling, so crawlers never see the `noindex` at `app/routes/dashboard.tsx:1`. This looks deliberate and harmless for a private page. Mentioned only for awareness. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Dynamic content:** `/api/changelog` isn't in the repository, so I can't see what it returns. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools and Bing to find the site, as `geo.config.json` says. - I sampled all 4 public routes. `/dashboard` is deliberately private and was left out of the route counts. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
